claims.text: Niobium can exhibit superconducting properties at cryogenic temperatures.
Refining and tailoring niobium grain boundaries will enhance its superconducting properties.
Thermomechanical processing followed by controlled annealing can produce smaller niobium grains.
Thermomechanical processing followed by controlled annealing can produce more uniform niobium grains and optimized grain boundaries.
Niobium grain-boundary refinement reduces grain-boundary scattering.
Smaller, more homogeneous niobium grains minimize electron-scattering sites.
Minimizing electron-scattering sites increases Cooper-pair coherence in niobium.
Increased Cooper-pair coherence raises the critical current density of niobium.
Increased Cooper-pair coherence could raise the critical temperature of niobium.
Microstructurally refined niobium will have lower electrical resistance at cryogenic temperatures than coarse-grained niobium.
Microstructurally refined niobium will have a modestly higher superconducting critical current density than coarse-grained niobium.
Excessively fine niobium grains could diminish the proposed superconducting improvements by introducing extrinsic scattering centers or stresses.
Contamination could diminish the proposed superconducting improvements by introducing extrinsic scattering centers or stresses.

contradictions.description: The intervention proposes smaller grains, which generally implies greater grain-boundary density, while the mediator and mechanism assert reduced grain-boundary scattering and fewer electron-scattering sites without explaining how the additional boundaries become less scattering.
